newsitem.title: USA: U.S. distillate output highest in three years-EIA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. distillate output highest in three years-EIA.

text.p: U.S. production of distillate jumped 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 3.6 million bpd, the highest one-week output in at least three years, the U.S. Energy Information Administration said Thursday.
But the EIA said demand of 3.6 million bpd nearly matched the output, and stocks fell 0.9 million barrels in the week ended October 11.
The season begins with total stocks 20.2 million barrels below last year, with East Coast stocks down 21.2 million barrels from the 58.8 million reported at this time last year.
U.S. diesel stocks were comparable to year-ago volumes, but heating oil was 27 percent lower. The major difference was in the East Coast, where heating oil stocks were down 43 percent, the EIA said.
Heating oil prices for the first 1996-97 heating survey were higher than prices a year ago averaging 109.5 cents per gallon, up 19.6 cents from the October 2, 1995 price.
Contributing factors to the jump in heating oil prices were the higher price of crude oil, up about $7 per barrel from a year ago, and low heating oil stocks.
